analysis.title: Cadence: Another beat/raise for high quality compounder on track for Rule of 65
key_insights: Cadence delivered its third FY26 guidance raise, most of it from 4Q. 4Q sales/EPS guide is +4%/+10% vs consensus per the report's framing. FY26E implies ~21% sales growth on 44.7% pro forma operating margin, above the 'Rule of 65' framework.
3Q26 results: sales $1.633bn and non-GAAP EPS $2.11 beat Street by +1%/+3%. Street sales were $1,613.7m and Street EPS was $2.05.
Cadence launched Maestro, a family of chip-design-specialized post-trained open-weight models. It adds a model layer on top of Cadence's agents and core design tools.
Cadence targets incremental pro forma operating margins of at least 50%. It averaged 54% across FY21-25, which BofA reads as conservative guidance.
Backlog rose to a record $8.2bn. cRPO was flat QoQ at $4.2bn ahead of the FY27E guide due in 4Q.

BofA raises FY27/28E pro forma EPS by +4%/+5% and sees out-year estimates as conservative relative to Synopsys, given limited long-term commentary from management and a record of beating and raising off prudent guidance.
PO stays $420, now based on 35x CY28E P/E (previously 44x CY27E). The stock trades at ~35x NTM P/E vs a 43x 3-year median.
Hardware posted another record quarter, with supply no longer a constraint. Demand is very strong across several large customers, including Intel.
Share gains are broadening beyond digital implementation: 16 full-flow digital wins in the quarter, plus displacements in analog (Spectre FX at 2nm) and PCB (Allegro at an EV OEM).
3Q buyback doubled to $400m and a new $2.5bn authorization is management's largest buyback increase. Cadence is on track to repurchase $1.2bn of shares in FY26E.

China upside (~15% of the $6.4bn current guide vs 12-13% of the initial $5.95bn, ~$200m upside) and Hexagon contribution (~$160m) account for ~80% of the FY26E raise since 4Q25. Growth excluding both is only 14%.

Reaching 50% pro forma operating margin by FY30E requires ~57% incremental margins vs the recent 54% average. Synopsys also targets 50% by FY30E, so Cadence's historical margin premium could narrow if Synopsys closes the profitability gap via Ansys synergies and IP royalties.
4Q26 guide: revenue $1,710m ($1,695m-$1,725m), non-GAAP operating margin 44.5% (44%-45%), non-GAAP EPS $2.22 ($2.19-$2.25).
Net cash was -$1,181m (-$4.29/share) at 3Q26 after cash was used for the $3.2bn Hexagon D&E acquisition. Free cash flow was $361.9m, a 22.2% margin, below Street's 42.8%.
3Q26 non-GAAP gross margin was 88.8% and non-GAAP operating margin 44.1% vs 44.0% Street. GAAP EPS was $1.05.

market_movers.rationale: Beat and raise quarter, record hardware and backlog, broadening share gains, and conservative out-year estimates relative to Synopsys. PO is on 35x CY28E P/E.

sector_views.rationale: EDA is levered to semiconductor secular trends with muted cyclicality. BofA sees Cadence as a defensive, scarce asset and a beneficiary of rising chip complexity.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported (10/2026): non-GAAP EPS $2.11 vs Street $2.05 and BofA $2.04, company guide $2.04 ($2.01-$2.07). GAAP EPS $1.05 reported vs Street $1.14.
3Q26 reported revenue $1,633.3m vs Street $1,613.7m, BofA $1,610.1m, guide $1,610m. Beat Street by $19.6m (+1.2%), +22.0% YoY, +3.1% QoQ.
3Q26 segments reported: EDA $1,127.0m (+18.6% YoY, vs BofA $1,115.1m), IP $245.0m (+22.0% YoY, vs BofA $247.2m).
4Q26 company guide: sales $1.710bn midpoint (range $1.695-1.725bn) vs Street est $1,648.2m, +3.8%. Non-GAAP EPS guide $2.22 midpoint vs Street est $2.02. BofA moved 4Q26E EPS from $1.99 to $2.23.

FY26E (BofA est): sales $6,402m (from $6,300m), non-GAAP EPS $8.41 (from $8.10) vs Bloomberg consensus $8.16. FY27E EPS $10.08 (from $9.57) vs consensus $9.55. FY28E EPS $11.84 (from $11.18) vs consensus $11.15.
FY27E sales raised to $7,361m from $7,196m and FY28E to $8,363m from $8,166m (BofA estimates).
3Q26 non-GAAP operating margin 44.1% vs company guide 44% and Street 44.0%. Non-GAAP opex $730.3m vs Street $704.7m.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CDNS, PO $420 on 35x CY28E P/E
trade_ideas.rationale: Beat/raise compounder with record hardware, broadening share gains, conservative estimates and a valuation of ~35x NTM P/E vs 43x 3Y median.
trade_ideas.risk: Share loss to primary competitors, semis R&D downturn, US-China trade war, semiconductor industry consolidation, and failure of the system analysis expansion.

risk_factors: Share loss in existing markets to primary competitors.
Broader economic downturn dampens semis R&D spending and corresponding EDA tools and services spend.
Escalation of US-China trade war limits ability to sell to key customers.
Semiconductor industry consolidation diminishes customer spending power.
Venture into the adjacent system analysis market fails to accelerate revenue growth, and incremental investment suppresses margin expansion.
China upside and Hexagon account for ~80% of the FY26E raise, with normalized growth of only 14%.
The path to 50% pro forma operating margin needs ~57% incremental margins vs the recent 54% average.
Synopsys could close the profitability gap, reducing Cadence's relative premium.
geopolitical: US-China trade war escalation is listed as a downside risk that could limit Cadence's ability to sell to key customers.
China contributed upside to FY26E guidance, now on track for ~15% of the current guide.

tension_points.bull_case: Third FY26 raise, FY26E ~21% growth on 44.7% pro forma operating margin, record backlog and hardware, broadening share gains, 54% average incremental margin vs 50% target, and conservative out-year estimates.
tension_points.bear_case: China upside and Hexagon account for ~80% of the FY26E raise, with normalized growth of 14%. Reaching 50% margin by FY30E needs ~57% incremental margins, and Synopsys could close the profitability gap.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Incremental operating margins falling short of the ~57% needed for 50% pro forma operating margin by FY30E, or Synopsys closing the profitability gap.

theme_stances.key_argument: Cadence has a strong record of beating and raising off prudent guidance, so out-year estimates look conservative relative to Synopsys.
theme_stances.evidence: strong track record of beat/raising off prudent guidance
